text: Mean-Shift Super-Resolution (MSSR; Torres-García et al. 2022, doi:10.1038/s41467-022-34693-9) subtracts local, range-weighted mean-shift estimate pixel refines result order steps. fwhm point-spread-function width input pixels default.  amplified grid adds samples. mssr_coords() places input-pixel units, field view stays [0.5, n + 0.5]: far separation go? Compare value midpoint two sources value source center, input MSSR map (values 1 mean dip sources): 3 px input shows shallow dip, MSSR deepens strongly. 2.4 px blurred sources form single hump, MSSR returns single, sharper hump: enhances existing structure split sources blur already merged.
code: g <- expand.grid(r = 1:31, c = 1:41) spot <- function(r0, c0, a = 1) a * exp(-((g$r - r0)^2 + (g$c - c0)^2) / (2 * (3 / 2.3548)^2)) pair <- function(sep) matrix(spot(16, 18) + spot(16, 18 + sep) + 0.05, 31, 41) x <- pair(3)                       # two sources 3 px apart, FWHM 3 px res <- mssr(x, fwhm = 3, amp = 2) res #> <mssr_result> intensity_weighted_structure #>   input 31 x 41 -> output 62 x 82 (amp 2, extent grid) #>   fwhm 3 px, order 1, kernel disk (half-size 3), mesh TRUE #>   engine mssr_r_rev2; zero fraction 0.488 #>   Not a quantitative intensity: measure on the original data. op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5)) show(x, "input"); show(as.matrix(res), "mssr(amp = 2)") par(op) range(mssr_coords(res)$col) #> [1]  0.75 41.25 res$transform$spacing #> row col  #> 0.5 0.5 mid_ratio <- function(sep) {   x <- pair(sep)   r <- mssr(x, fwhm = 3, amp = 2)   v <- as.matrix(r)   co <- mssr_coords(r)   row <- which.min(abs(co$row - 16))   at_input <- function(cc) stats::approx(1:41, x[16, ], cc)$y   at_mssr <- function(cc) stats::approx(co$col, v[row, ], cc)$y   c(input = at_input(18 + sep / 2) / at_input(18), mssr = at_mssr(18 + sep / 2) / at_mssr(18)) } round(rbind(`2.4 px` = mid_ratio(2.4), `3 px` = mid_ratio(3)), 3) #>        input  mssr #> 2.4 px 1.086 1.235 #> 3 px   0.968 0.255

title: mssrscopR 0.1.0
text: First functional version: single-frame Mean-Shift Super-Resolution (mssr()) explicit result objects (role, grid transform, parameters, engine identity mssr_r_rev2, diagnostics). mssr_coords() returns output pixel-center coordinates input-pixel units. mssr_mask() derives exact-count structural masks input grid seeded tie-breaking reports share decided tie-breaking. mssr_selftest() recomputes bundled synthetic fixtures regression check installation. Defined results degenerate input: flat frames return flagged zeros every amplification, undefined refinement steps (impulses exactly zero background) leave map unchanged counted. Classed cli errors (mssrscopR_error_*) warnings (mssrscopR_warning_negative); guards output size, kernel size total work.
